To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Drug consumption in monkeys responding under a schedule of drug injection was inversely related overall to unit price, but was not uniform at the same unit price.

(1) opioid consumption by rhesus monkeys decreased as unit-price increased; (2) the Hursh et al (1988) model and the linear model predicting consumption based on dose fit our data equally well; and (3) consumption was not uniform across unit prices.
the consumption of opioids by monkeys is a function of unit price, but the unit-price model does not predict consumption at a given unit cost.
